message.content:
READ-ONLY analysis. Do NOT edit any files. Working dir: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TS customer portal, "Nxeon" VPS hosting).

Read each of these CUSTOMER dashboard page files IN FULL and analyze:
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx  (944 lines — read all; invoices are merged in as a tab here)
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/invoices/page.tsx  (NOTE: standalone route, but nav says invoices merged into billing tab — check redundancy)
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/invoices/[id]/page.tsx
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/refer/page.tsx  (nav "Refer & earn")
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/affiliate/page.tsx  (NOTE: nav says Refer + Affiliate merged — check redundancy with refer)
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/team/page.tsx
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/team/accept/page.tsx
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/support/page.tsx
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/support/[id]/page.tsx
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/feedback/page.tsx  (NOTE: nav says Support + Feedback merged — check redundancy)
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/activity/page.tsx  (only 50 lines)
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/settings/page.tsx
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/tools/page.tsx  (index of 15 free micro-tools)

Also: the /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/tools/ subdir has 15 tiny page.tsx files (~10 lines each, e.g. base64, whois, port-checker). Read 3-4 of them (e.g. tools/whois/page.tsx, tools/json-formatter/page.tsx, tools/my-ip/page.tsx) to judge whether they're real or thin stubs, and generalize.

Context to check: is standalone /dashboard/invoices redundant with the billing tab? Is /dashboard/affiliate redundant with /dashboard/refer? Is /dashboard/feedback redundant with support?

For EACH route report, terse bullets:
- Coherent/current? (yes/partial/no)
- Dead / stale / redundant UI (placeholder text, "coming soon", disabled buttons, TODO, hardcoded/mock data, commented-out blocks)
- UX gaps (missing empty/loading/error states, no confirmation, dead-ends, redundancy with a sibling route)
- Half-finished / orphaned pieces
- Concrete improvement tagged P1 (broken/misleading/blocks money flow), P2 (notable gap/inconsistency), P3 (polish)

Cite exact file paths + line numbers/snippets for load-bearing findings. Be specific. Do NOT write any report file — return findings directly as your final message in structured markdown grouped by route.

content.text:
I have everything I need. Here are my findings.

---

# Customer Dashboard Route Audit — /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard

## Cross-cutting finding: the "merged" nav claim is false for all three merges

`app/dashboard/layout.tsx:76-85` builds the Account nav with a comment (`:78-79`) asserting three consolidations:
> `// Billing + Invoices merged (invoices live as a tab on the billing page); Refer & earn + Affiliate merged; Support + Feedback merged.`

None are actually merged. In every case the second route still exists as a full standalone page, absent from the nav, reachable only via a small text cross-link on its sibling. This is a half-finished consolidation: someone updated the nav comment and dropped three items from the sidebar, then wired cross-links instead of merging. Concretely:
- Invoices: **no tab exists** on billing — it's a preview card (see below). `/dashboard/invoices` is fully alive and linked twice from billing.
- Affiliate: `/dashboard/affiliate` not in nav; only entry is the refer-page cross-link.
- Feedback: `/dashboard/feedback` not in nav; only entry is the support-page cross-link.

**P2** — Either finish the merge (true tabs / a single route) or restore the nav entries. Right now `/dashboard/affiliate` and `/dashboard/feedback` are effectively orphaned routes discoverable only by a one-line hyperlink, and the nav comment describes a state that doesn't exist in the code.

---

## /dashboard/billing/page.tsx
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. The most mature page in the set — every recurring figure is priced through the single `renewalCharge` authority (`:168-208`), with extensive comments documenting past mispricing incidents. Impersonation guards, dunning, bandwidth-metering honesty, tax-inclusive totals all handled carefully.
- **Dead/stale/redundant UI:**
  - Two links to the same standalone invoices route on one page: top-of-page `:258` "View & download invoices →" and bottom card `:892` "View all". Redundant.
  - `CouponField` is deliberately hidden when Stripe is configured (`:466`) because the card path never redeems coupons — honest, documented, not a bug, but means the promo field is dead on any Stripe install.
  - `AutoRecharge` import carries a long historical comment (`:20-25`); the feature is correctly gated to card-on-file accounts (`:605-618`). Fine.
- **UX gaps:** No inline "pay this now" for an OPEN invoice from here — settlement is per-server via `SettleNowButton` (`:338`), which is correct for the model but means invoice-centric users have no pay button. The nav's promised "invoices tab" does not exist; it's a **preview card capped at 5** (`:92-96`, `:885-941`).
- **Half-finished/orphaned:** None internally.
- **Improvements:**
  - **P3** — Drop one of the two duplicate links to `/dashboard/invoices` (`:258` vs `:892`).
  - **P2** — Reconcile the nav comment: billing has no tabs; call it a preview or build a real tab.

## /dashboard/invoices/page.tsx (standalone)
- **Coherent/current?** Yes.
- **Redundancy check:** **Not truly redundant** with the billing card. This is the superset "view all": 200 invoices vs 5, stat tiles (`:41-45`), a Method column with card-snapshot fallback (`:83-94`), and **both** PDF and HTML download (`:101-102`) where billing only offers one download button. It's the legitimate detail target of billing's preview. Keep it — but it should either be in the nav or the billing comment shouldn't claim it's "a tab."
- **UX gaps:** No filter/search/pagination across up to 200 rows; minor at this scale.
- **Improvements:** **P3** — add status filter if invoice volume grows.

## /dashboard/invoices/[id]/page.tsx
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. Clean, correct ownership check (`:29` `notFound()` on mismatch), shared number formatter, tax/refund lines, payment-method snapshot with legacy fallback (`:73`).
- **UX gaps:** An **OPEN** invoice detail offers only Download buttons — **no "Pay" CTA**. A customer landing here on an unpaid invoice has no action; they must know to go settle the underlying server on billing.
- **Improvements:** **P2** — for `status === "OPEN"`, surface a pay/settle CTA (or a line explaining payment happens automatically from wallet), so the detail page isn't a dead-end for unpaid invoices.

## /dashboard/refer/page.tsx
- **Coherent/current?** Yes, but it is the "lite" half of a duplicated referral system.
- **Redundancy check:** **Genuinely redundant with /dashboard/affiliate.** Both:
  - reimplement the identical `ensureReferralCode` helper (`refer:11-27` ≈ `affiliate:18-34`) — copy-pasted;
  - render the same referral link + code + referred-count;
  - cross-link each other (`refer:45` → affiliate; `affiliate:250` → refer), so the user bounces between two pages describing the same action.
  - **Conflicting money narrative (load-bearing):** refer promises a **flat both-sided credit** of `referralRewardCents()` (default **$5**, `lib/growth.ts:13-19`). Affiliate advertises **per-referral commission tiers** — Starter $5 / **Pro $8 / Elite $12** (`lib/affiliate.ts:45-51`) — yet `computeAffiliateEarnings` derives actual earnings by summing wallet transactions tagged `"Referral bonus — you referred a friend"` (`lib/affiliate.ts:88-99`), i.e. **the same flat $5 credits the refer program creates.** So the affiliate tier table showing $8/$12 per referral is decorative copy that the crediting path may never actually pay. Same underlying reward pool, two contradictory descriptions.
- **Improvements:**
  - **P1** — Verify the referral-crediting code is tier-aware. If credits are always flat `referralRewardCents`, the affiliate page's "$8 / $12 per referral" tiers are a **misleading money claim** on a customer-facing page.
  - **P2** — Collapse refer + affiliate into one page (affiliate is the strict superset) and delete the duplicated `ensureReferralCode`.

## /dashboard/affiliate/page.tsx
- **Coherent/current?** Partial — functional, but see redundancy/conflict above.
- **Dead/stale/redundant UI:** Duplicated `ensureReferralCode` (`:18-34`). Whole page is a superset duplicate of refer.
- **Code smell:** A customer-facing page imports its payout form from an **admin** path: `import { PayoutRequestForm } from "@/components/admin/AffiliateControls"` (`:13`). Not broken, but misplaced — customer UI depending on an admin component module.
- **UX gaps:** Not in nav; only reachable via the refer cross-link. Two "status" vocabularies (referral converted/pending vs payout PENDING/APPROVED/PAID/DECLINED) on one page — acceptable but dense.
- **Improvements:** **P2** — merge with refer (canonical); move `PayoutRequestForm` out of `components/admin/` into a shared/customer module.

## /dashboard/team/page.tsx
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. Strong. Notable security discipline: co-member `userId` is never sent to the client (`:50-52`), email addresses gated to admins + self (`:57`), role/remove keyed by membership id. Documents a fixed P0 TOTP oracle.
- **Dead/stale/redundant UI:** None.
- **Improvements:** None material. **P3** — the substantive UI lives in `TeamManager` (client); no server-side empty state, but the client presumably handles the no-org case.

## /dashboard/team/accept/page.tsx
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. Model is correct: page only *describes* the invite; joining is a separate authenticated action (`acceptInvite`), re-checking every condition (`:24-65`). Good handling of wrong-account (`:42-45`, deliberately doesn't leak org name), expired/invalid, revoked-inviter, deleted-org.
- **Improvements:** None.

## /dashboard/support/page.tsx
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. Single shared reply-time promise (`SUPPORT_REPLY_SENTENCE`) fixing a past inconsistency (`:28-30`). Proper empty state, priority tones, message counts.
- **Redundancy check:** Cross-links feedback (`:31`). Support (tickets) vs feedback (bug/feature board) are **distinct concepts — not truly redundant**; the only problem is the false "merged" nav claim.
- **Improvements:** **P3** — none functional.

## /dashboard/support/[id]/page.tsx
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. Chat-style staff/customer bubbles, admin can view any ticket (`:26`), reply form suppressed on CLOSED with reopen hint (`:64-73`).
- **Improvements:** None material.

## /dashboard/feedback/page.tsx
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. Bug/feature board with status lifecycle (NEW/PLANNED/IN_PROGRESS/DONE/DECLINED) and admin reply notes (`:67-71`). Proper empty state.
- **Redundancy check:** Not redundant with support (different data model — public roadmap-style feedback vs private tickets). Only issue is nav discoverability (orphaned; see cross-cutting).
- **Improvements:** **P2** — restore to nav or genuinely merge under Support; currently only reachable via one hyperlink.

## /dashboard/activity/page.tsx
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. 50-line audit-log timeline, humanized actions, dot colors, empty state (`:21-26`), capped at 100 (`:14`).
- **Improvements:** **P3** — no pagination/"load more" beyond 100; fine for now.

## /dashboard/settings/page.tsx
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. Server-rendered `?tab=` tabs (Profile / Security / Integrations / Notifications), account overview, profile/password/SSH, 2FA + API tokens, Cloudflare + Anthropic BYOK integrations (stable deep-link anchor `#anthropic-key`, `:187-191`), danger zone. Rich and consistent.
- **Dead/stale/redundant UI:** None found.
- **Improvements:** None material.

## /dashboard/tools/page.tsx + subpages — REAL, not stubs
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. The index is catalog-driven (`TOOLS.length`, `toolsByCategory()`), 4 categories, In-browser badges (`:48-52`).
- **Are the tiny pages real?** **Real.** Each ~10-line `page.tsx` (whois, json-formatter, my-ip, etc.) is a thin *route wrapper* that renders a fully-implemented client component reused from the marketing suite via the shared `_ToolPage` chrome (`_ToolPage.tsx`). Example: `MyIpTool` (`components/marketing/tools/MyIpTool.tsx`) does a real `fetch("/api/tools/my-ip")` with loading/error/result states and copy button. Thin files, real functionality — a deliberate reuse pattern, not stubs.
- **Minor discrepancy (not a bug):** Task said "15 tools"; there are **16 tool subdirs** and **18 catalog slugs** (`lib/tools/catalog.ts`). The index renders the count dynamically from `TOOLS.length`, so it's self-consistent regardless.
- **Improvements:** **P3** — none.

---

### Priority summary
- **P1 (verify — potential misleading money claim):** Affiliate tier copy advertises $8/$12 per referral (`lib/affiliate.ts:45-51`) while actual earnings are summed from flat-$5 referral wallet credits (`lib/affiliate.ts:88-99` + `lib/growth.ts:13-19`); confirm the crediting path is tier-aware or the tiers are false advertising.
- **P2:** (1) refer/affiliate are duplicate referral systems with contradictory reward narratives — merge; (2) nav claims 3 merges that don't exist — finish or restore Affiliate + Feedback nav entries; (3) OPEN invoice detail has no pay CTA (dead-end); (4) `PayoutRequestForm` mis-located under `components/admin/`.
- **P3:** duplicate invoices links on billing; invoices/activity pagination; billing "invoices tab" wording (it's a preview card).

Standout: `billing/page.tsx` is genuinely high-quality (single pricing authority, honest metering). The rot is concentrated in the abandoned refer↔affiliate and support↔feedback "merges."
